evals.prompt: We have about a million contract and invoice files in Postgres. Users ask questions like which payments belong to a company through its contracts and invoices — the chain is never in one file. Design the retrieval layer. Do not write application code.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs inventory (or states repo scan + Gate 1 fields), chooses relational GraphRAG because N≥2 hops and no single document contains the chain, fills a Retrieval Design Report (DDL, provenance edges, traversal caps, eval gates), does not implement application code. If ns-graphrag is installed: requires GraphRAG Process Report before ns-spec-driven; if absent: retrieval-only handoff with process gaps open.
assertions: Chooses relational GraphRAG (entity/edge), not vector-only as the primary mode
States N≥2 hops and that no single document contains the chain
Includes or requires a Corpus Inventory (volume, archetypes, or equivalent Gate 1)
Produces or fills a Retrieval Design Report (or equivalent structured report)
Does not implement application code / refuses to write app workers or HTTP
If ns-graphrag installed: Process Report before ns-spec-driven; if absent: retrieval-only handoff with process gaps noted

evals.prompt: Small internal knowledge base, a few thousand markdown notes. We only need topic search — find similar notes. Should we add a graph?
evals.expected_output: Agent recommends vector-only, refuses graph tables, still requires Gate 1 inventory at appropriate scale, may mention pgvector HNSW; no GraphRAG, no application code.
assertions: Recommends vector-only (or equivalent semantic/pgvector search without graph tables)
Explicitly refuses or rejects adding entity/edge / GraphRAG for this case
Does not prescribe multi-hop traversal as required
Does not write application implementation code

evals.prompt: Our current schema stores nearest-neighbor rows as if they were relationships — we INSERT an edge whenever cosine similarity is high. Retrieval sometimes invents links between companies and payments. Diagnose and tell us what to change in the design. No application code.
evals.expected_output: Agent diagnoses similarity-as-link anti-pattern, requires entity resolution (candidates vs confirmed edges with provenance), lists eval gates (false-link rate, path precision), points to anti-patterns / entity-resolution / evaluation refs; does not treat distance as sufficient for an edge.
assertions: Diagnoses treating vector similarity as a stored link / edge as an anti-pattern
Requires entity resolution: vector = candidate only; edge needs key/rule + provenance
Mentions false-link rate or path precision (or equivalent eval gates)
Cites anti-patterns, entity-resolution, or evaluation-and-gates doctrine

evals.prompt: Two million documents split across legal contracts and engineering runbooks — one pgvector index returns wrong-domain neighbors on half our queries. We still need hybrid search within each domain. Design retrieval. No app code.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs Gate 1 inventory, locks hybrid as base mode, enables multi-index augmentation with measured symptom (domain contamination), requires deterministic index-routing key aligned to ADR Gateway intent categories, cross-index fan-out only as explicit fallback tier; fills Retrieval Design Report with augmentation fields; refuses agentic or both without separate symptom.
assertions: Chooses hybrid as base mode (not vector-only or GraphRAG as primary)
Enables multi-index augmentation with domain-contamination symptom
Requires deterministic index-routing key (not fan-out every query)
Links routing key to Gateway intent category (same taxonomy, not second taxonomy)
Does not stack agentic augmentation without its own measured symptom
Fills or requires Retrieval Design Report with augmentation lock fields

evals.prompt: Our RAG team wants multi-index, agentic retrieval loops, and GraphRAG tables on a 5k-note FAQ — no measured symptoms yet, just future-proofing. What do you recommend?
evals.expected_output: Agent refuses unjustified stacking: vector-only base mode, augmentations none, no GraphRAG tables; cites retrieval-augmentations anti-patterns (all patterns for later without symptom); still requires Gate 1 inventory at appropriate scale.
assertions: Recommends vector-only base mode for small FAQ topic search
Sets augmentations to none — refuses multi-index and agentic without measured symptoms
Refuses GraphRAG / entity-edge tables for this case
Cites anti-pattern of enabling augmentations for later without symptom
Does not write application implementation code
